newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends higher on soy, corn surge.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends higher on soy, corn surge.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled higher on spillover strength from a weather-related surge in CBOT corn and soybeans, traders said.
Corn and soybeans rallied sharply higher on concern that very hot, dry weather in the U.S. Midwest could hinder crop development.

"It was hectic early and then it just kind of tapered off until the close. We were up in line with everybody else, and then at the end we saw (Benson-Quinn) buying 400,000 Sept bushels. That helped us close relatively higher than the other wheat markets," an MGE trader said.
MGE spring wheat settled seven to 11 cents per bushel higher, with new crop September up 10 cents at $3.66-3/4. Earlier in the session, September was up 16-1/4 cents at $3.73.

Traders said Benson-Quinn, Atwood-Peavey, Country Hedging and Prudential each bought at least one million Sept bushels. CIS sold 1.2 million Sept and Prudential sold 1.6 million Sept and one million Dec.
The MGE estimated Monday's spring wheat futures volume at 16.385 million bushels.
